source_admission: Primary experimental studies checked on 2026-10-09. No paper or external data bytes are redistributed. Access states which portions were actually read. Derived coefficients and their transfer to a hypothetical floater remain conditional; none is a measured floater trait.

sources.citation: van Iersel, M. W. and Seymour, L. (2000). Growth Respiration, Maintenance Respiration, and Carbon Fixation of Vinca: A Time Series Analysis. Journal of the American Society for Horticultural Science 125, 702–706.
sources.access: Publisher PDF abstract, methods, coefficient definitions and results inspected.
sources.evidence: Whole-plant gas exchange supports model-derived construction cost 1.39 g glucose/g dry material and maintenance 0.031 g glucose/g dry material/day.
sources.boundary: Seedlings at 22/18 C and 14/10-hour light/dark conditions; root-zone fluxes included. Coefficients depend on physiology and composition. They cannot be applied to an inert envelope or used to validate lunar-night survival.

sources.citation: van Iersel, M. W. (2003). Carbon use efficiency depends on growth respiration, maintenance respiration, and relative growth rate. A case study with lettuce. Plant, Cell & Environment 26, 1441–1449.
sources.access: Publisher full HTML: carbon equations, measurements and fitted-coefficient comparisons inspected.
sources.evidence: Different fits to lettuce data gave maintenance 31–39 mg glucose/g dry matter/day and construction respiration 0.40–0.62 g glucose/g new dry matter.
sources.boundary: Construction respiration is not the total construction substrate. Maintenance and carbon-use efficiency vary with size and growth; these are active terrestrial plant references, not universal lower bounds.

sources.citation: Melis, A., Zhang, L., Forestier, M., Ghirardi, M. L. and Seibert, M. (2000). Sustained photobiological hydrogen gas production upon reversible inactivation of oxygen evolution in the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. Plant Physiology 122, 127–136.
sources.access: Original abstract through PubMed, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10631256/; PMC full text blocked.
sources.evidence: Sulfur deprivation separates oxygenic growth and sustained hydrogen production in culture.
sources.boundary: A physiological switch with recovery and substrate requirements, not continuous simultaneous normal growth and unlimited hydrogen synthesis.

sources.citation: Kosourov, S., Jokel, M., Aro, E.-M. and Allahverdiyeva, Y. (2018). A new approach for sustained and efficient H2 photoproduction by Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. Energy & Environmental Science 11, 1431–1436.
sources.access: Publisher-indexed search excerpts and original abstract read; direct full-HTML retrieval failed.
sources.evidence: Pulse illumination supports hydrogen production with a reported early light-energy conversion peak around 1.6–1.7%; cells did not grow under that pulse regime.
sources.boundary: The efficiency denominator, pulse duty and short measurement period prevent direct substitution into annual all-solar production. The evaluation's efficiency sweep is hypothetical, not a calibration from that peak.

sources.citation: Kosourov, S. et al. (2020). Water oxidation by photosystem II is the primary source of electrons for sustained H2 photoproduction in nutrient-replete green algae. PNAS 117, 29629–29636.
sources.access: Publisher HTML significance, abstract, isotope results and carbon-fixation competition sections inspected.
sources.evidence: Direct water biophotolysis established under microoxic pulsed illumination; in the examined efficient regime, carbon fixation was inactive.
sources.boundary: Oxygen consumption, hydrogen uptake and measurement conditions matter. Productive H2 organs cannot receive an additional full carbon-fixation credit for those same absorbed photons.

sources.citation: Liran, O. et al. (2016). Microoxic Niches within the Thylakoid Stroma of Air-Grown Chlamydomonas reinhardtii Protect [FeFe]-Hydrogenase and Support Hydrogen Production under Fully Aerobic Environment. Plant Physiology 172, 264–271.
sources.access: Publisher HTML abstract, oxygen-uptake results and discussion inspected.
sources.evidence: Oxygen-consuming microenvironments preserve hydrogenase function in air-grown cells; hydrogen release increases transiently under brighter light.
sources.boundary: The reported hydrogen branch used less than 1% of the initial electron flow. This refutes an absolute oxygen prohibition but does not establish balloon-scale output or its long-term resource cost.

sources.citation: Masset, J. et al. (2012). Fermentative hydrogen production from glucose and starch using pure strains and artificial co-cultures of Clostridium spp. Biotechnology for Biofuels 5, 35.
sources.access: Publisher full HTML: fixed-pH glucose experiments, repeated-batch yields, product composition and partial-pressure discussion inspected.
sources.evidence: Measured glucose yields included 2.1 mol H2/mol glucose; repeated culture varied from 1.63 to 2.32. Biogas contained 62–65% H2; fatty acids accumulated.
sources.boundary: Regulated anaerobic reactors; high H2 partial pressure and metabolite accumulation affect performance. Four mol/mol is the ideal acetate-pathway comparison, not a demonstrated organism efficiency or a limit for all light-assisted pathways.

declared_sensitivities.maintenance: 0.001, 0.003, 0.01 and 0.031 kg glucose/kg living dry tissue/day. Only the last is directly anchored to the selected whole-vinca estimate; the lower values explore less costly tissue or suppression and are not established lunar physiology.
declared_sensitivities.light_and_gpp: GPP 1, 3 and 5 kg C/m2/year, mean incident power 100 W/m2, and matched-basis light-to-H2 efficiencies 0.5%, 1% and 2% are imposed comparisons. No floater optical/photosynthesis model supplies them yet.
declared_sensitivities.night: Night metabolic fractions 0.1, 0.25 and 1 are selected sensitivities. Reserves are separate carbohydrate mass; maintaining living tissue creates a nonzero demand floor.
declared_sensitivities.chemistry: Glucose carbon mass fraction 0.4 and starch fraction 4/9 are stoichiometric approximations. Hydrogen/glucose molar masses 0.002016/0.180156 kg/mol are exposed conversion inputs, not adjustable physiological yields.
declared_sensitivities.reproduction: Recruitment probability, reproductive lifetime, bud construction, nutrients, reserves and gas acquisition must all be supplied explicitly. A positive carbon balance alone does not supply a life cycle.
